loading.note: Volume scaling by k is the correct FFE->TEU direction
Revenue rate scaled by k instead of divided by k. Combined with F-01 the product carries k^2. Reproduced by direct arithmetic; two independent computations agree to 10 significant figures.
Per-FFE rate -> per-TEU rate. Verified against all 47 WorldSmall ports.
Only port column not scaled; correctly, since it is per call
Applied unconditionally on the JSON path. Docstring claims a WorldSmall exemption that does not exist in code. Revenue is NOT scaled, creating a 6x revenue/cost skew.
Arithmetic is unit-clean. The defect is scope, not formula: each region is checked against the full unpartitioned fleet.

service_ga.note: Formula is a correct weighted mean; its input revenue_per_teu carries the k^2 defect.
service_direct_demand[i] credits each lane to EVERY service covering both endpoints (service_ga.py:134-138). Implied served volume 296,310 TEU/wk vs 276,446.80 true = 1.0719x over-count.
Range (0.6, 1.0]. It is a utilization discount, correctly implemented. Named misleadingly.
Applies ONE network-average rate to all lanes. Lane profitability differences never enter service selection.

service_ga.formula: port_cost += served * handling_cost + fixed_cost + served * variable_cost
service_ga.note: served is the service-total load, applied once per port in the loop. Per-TEU rates should multiply the load at THAT port.
hub_ratio derived from num_hubs = 0.1 * num_ports, clamped to [0.3, 0.7]. Heuristic, undocumented.
total_capacity OMITS the 7/cycle_time factor that F-10 applies to served. Overcapacity penalty is computed on capacity that does not exist.

service_ga.formula: profit = revenue - operating - fuel - transship - port - unserved_pen - overcap_pen - alignment_pen - neg_svc_pen
fitness = sum(weight * value) for all components incl. cost
service_ga.note: No sign handling. Operating cost carries a POSITIVE coefficient, so the GA rewards higher operating cost.
Sign is correct but guarded by objective_mode=='legacy'; production mode is 'profit_first'. CONFIG weights (0.60/0.25/0.15) reach service_ga.w_* and are consumed ONLY here.

service_ga.formula: service_cost = weekly_cost + service_fuel + (served * port_hc if 'port_hc' in locals() else 0)
service_ga.note: port_hc is a stale loop variable retaining the LAST port processed. Drives the negative-margin penalty ladder against one arbitrary port's rate.
Identical inputs and identical function. Pure waste; the two values can never be reconciled if either changes.

frequency_ga.note: Named avg_ but assigns a single arbitrary lane's rate. service_ga.py:146 computes the true average in another module; it is not shared.

frequency_ga.formula: fitness = revenue - operating_cost - transship_cost - overcap_penalty - port_cost
frequency_ga.note: fuel_cost is computed at :161-166 then OMITTED from the return. The frequency optimizer is blind to the dominant cost term.

frequency_ga.formula: vessels_used = ceil(cycle_time * f / 7); reject if > fleet_size (returns -1e9)
frequency_ga.note: This fleet check WORKS. fleet_size resolves to problem.fleet.total_vessels = 263 on the production path. Recorded to correct an earlier working assumption.

hub_milp.formula: max Pi = REV - OPEX - FUEL - TRANS - PORT - alpha*sum(u) + COVBONUS
hub_milp.note: Objective is not profit. See F-31 and F-37.

hub_milp.formula: REV = sum_d sum_s r_d * x_ds + sum_d sum_(s1,s2) r_d * t_d,s1,s2
hub_milp.note: Only lane-specific revenue model in the system. Inherits k^2 from F-02.

hub_milp.formula: OPEX = sum_{s in A} svc.weekly_cost * max(1, round(freq[s]))
hub_milp.note: Python CONSTANT, not an LP expression. Critically: sums over services_mask WITHOUT port filtering, so every cluster's MILP re-bills every active service. Measured inflation of reported operating_cost vs per-service detail: 1.311x (Asia), 1.968x (Europe), 1.365x (Americas).

hub_milp.formula: FUEL = sum_{s in A} calculate_weekly_fuel_cost(s.ports, ...) * max(1, round(freq[s]))
hub_milp.note: Python CONSTANT. Same missing port filter as F-29 (measured 1.290x / 1.833x / 1.318x inflation). No fleet constraint bounds frequency. Reported total is 11.71x the entire 263-vessel fleet's physical maximum burn.
Rate depends only on the demand lane's endpoints; the hub h actually used is ignored. Same rate regardless of routing.

hub_milp.formula: PORT = sum_p [ h_p * sum(v) + sum(v * phi_p) + pi_p * sum_s f_s ]
hub_milp.note: port_flow_direct[p].append(var) at :337 appends the SAME variable once per port on the route, so per-TEU handling+variable is charged once PER PORT. A 2-port service pays twice; a 7-port hub loop pays 7x. Hub loops list the hub twice (service_generator_agent.py:165), charging the hub 2x per TEU. Separately, transfer_flow vars are never added to port_flow_direct, so a transshipped TEU pays zero handling at any port.

Multiplicative in operating cost. Raising cost raises the objective. Reduces to a linear per-TEU bonus lambda = (w_c/w_p)*(OPEX+1)/D_tot, which GROWS with service count - the model can buy coverage by inflating the service count.

Both operands are Python ints, so this is a bool. Empirically verified against pulp 2.7.0: True case silently adds ZERO constraints; False case raises TypeError: A False object cannot be passed as a constraint. fleet_size hardcoded at 300 (hub_milp.py:61), never overridden - GA uses 263. A violation therefore CRASHES solve() and regional_agent.py:381-395 converts it to a zero-profit fallback region.

hub_milp.formula: C1: sum_s x_ds + sum t_d,s1,s2 + u_d == D_d
hub_milp.note: Correct equality. Every TEU is shipped, transferred, or explicitly unserved. The one structurally sound part of the MILP.
min_coverage defaults to 0.0 (hub_milp.py:56) AND regional_agent.py:31 passes MIN_COVERAGE_FLOOR = 0.0. Condition 'if self.min_coverage > 0' never true. Verified by grep across src/.

hub_milp.formula: C3: sum x + sum t <= C_s * f_s * (7/cycle_time)
hub_milp.note: Correctly applies the same 7/cycle_time normalization as the revenue side, so capacity and demand are scaled consistently.
demand_score sums weekly_teu over BOTH origin and destination roles, double-counting. Binds only when score > 55,556. WorldSmall max = 39,722 (DEBRV). Zero ports qualify. Decorative.
Returns REV - ... + COVBONUS, i.e. includes the cost-proportional coverage bonus. This is what is reported as profit.
Warn-only, then returns a full result anyway. Also unreachable: control flow cannot reach it with total_vessels_used > fleet_size because line 389 would already have raised.
Verified consequence: every regional_results[*].revenue in the artifact is 0.00. Per-region revenue is structurally absent.

orchestrator.formula: true_global_demand = sum(d.weekly_teu for d in problem.demands)

orchestrator.note: satisfied clamped at TWO levels (regional_agent.py:442 and here); unserved clamped at NEITHER. Result: satisfied+unserved = 305,021.20 vs true 276,446.80 = +10.34% phantom. Coverage understated 9.26pp.
Arithmetic is correct; the numerator is corrupted upstream by F-43.

TAUTOLOGY. Substituting profit = revenue - cost yields revenue == revenue. Revenue carries zero independent information and cannot be falsified. The accompanying comment (unserved penalty captured in operating cost) is factually false.
Cluster demands are selected with 'd.origin in cluster OR d.destination in cluster' (:349-352), so cross-cluster lanes appear in TWO independent MILPs. satisfied is clamped; unserved is not.

fuel_model.note: consumption comes from the hardcoded VESSEL_FUEL_CONSUMPTION table, not from fleet_data.csv 'Bunker ton per day at designSpeed'. Table speed values are 1.19-1.35x the fleet file's designSpeed.

fuel_model.note: Silent 500nm substitution. Never triggers on WorldSmall (47/47 ports present). Fires for 227 of 435 WorldLarge ports.
All 263 vessels underway 24/7 at design consumption. Reported fuel is 11.71x this bound.
